result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is from your eye surgeon. It is written to your eye doctor (optometrist). It is about the check of both your eyes.

- Your vision is 20/40 in the right eye. It is 20/50 in the left eye.
- You have a dense cataract in each eye (3 to 4+ nuclear sclerotic).
- Your loss of vision seems to be caused by the cataracts in both eyes.
- You have mild guttata in both eyes. This may be early Fuchs dystrophy. It is only possible, not confirmed.
- Your eye pressure is 12 mmHg in both eyes.
- There is no relative afferent pupillary defect.
- The vitreous, macula, vessels and edges of the eye look normal. The cup-to-disc ratio is 0.1 in both eyes.
- The surgeon says you should do well with cataract surgery.

## What you need to do
1. The surgeon recommended cataract surgery. You agreed to have the first eye done shortly.
2. Ask the surgeon's office when your surgery will be. The letter gives no date.

## Dates and medicines
- Surgery date for the first eye: not given. The letter only says "shortly".
- The letter lists no medicines.
- The surgeon will update your eye doctor after surgery on each eye.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my first eye surgery be?
- What are guttata, and what does "possible early Fuchs dystrophy" mean for me?
- What will happen after surgery on each eye?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
